name: Traditional Fado Dinner Show
seoTitle: Alfama Fado Dinners: Prices, Timings and House Rules
tagline: How a fado dinner in Alfama works: timings, prices, etiquette and how to pick a house.

description.short: A fado dinner is an evening at a casa de fado, where sets of live fado alternate with the courses. This guide explains timings, how pricing works, the etiquette and how to tell a good house from a tourist trap, for passengers whose ship stays into the evening.
description.full:
A fado dinner is an evening commitment, so it suits passengers whose ship stays late or overnight in Lisbon. Most fado houses open for dinner around 19:30 to 20:00 and the singing starts around 20:30 to 21:00, in short sets that alternate with the courses until midnight or later. If all-aboard is before about 23:00, you will catch only the first sets.

Alfama is the obvious choice from the ship: many houses are within a 5 to 15 minute walk of the terminal, uphill into the lanes behind the river. Bairro Alto and other districts also have fado houses, but mean a taxi back.

How the money works: established houses usually charge a fixed set menu that includes the performance, rather than an entry ticket. In 2026 two long-running Alfama houses publish set menus of €68 (Parreirinha de Alfama) and €78 (Clube de Fado) per person; at Clube de Fado drinks are extra. Smaller tascas, where the singing is often amateur fado vadio, usually work on a minimum spend instead and cost less. Always ask what the minimum per person is, and whether drinks are included, before you sit down.

Etiquette is simple. When the lights dim and a singer stands, stop talking, put the phone away and pause your meal. Service stops during each fado. Applaud at the end of each song, and talk and order between sets.

To judge a house, look for a published menu and price, musicians on Portuguese guitar and classical guitar (viola), and silence kept during the singing. Be wary of people recruiting diners in the street for 'fado shows', of houses that will not state a price, and of loud rooms where the music is background to the meal. Book a day or more ahead in summer.

If your ship leaves before evening, the Fado Museum on Largo do Chafariz de Dentro, a few minutes' walk from the terminal, is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–18:00 (€5).
description.history: Fado took shape in Lisbon in the first half of the 19th century, sung in taverns and streets in working-class neighbourhoods such as Alfama and Mouraria. Its first legend was Maria Severa, a singer from Mouraria who died in 1846. In the 20th century, licensing rules and the growth of radio, records and film moved fado into dedicated casas de fado with professional singers, and Amália Rodrigues (1920–1999) took it to international audiences. Parreirinha de Alfama, licensed from 1939, is one of the houses from that era still open. In 2011 UNESCO inscribed fado as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, and the Fado Museum in Alfama, opened in 1998, documents its history.
description.significance: Fado is Lisbon's own urban song and the live music most visitors hear in the city. Its subjects are local: the river and the sea, the old neighbourhoods, love and loss, and saudade, a longing for what is absent. A good fado house is one of the few places where you hear it as intended, close up, with the room silent. That is also why a noisy, overpriced one is such a disappointment.

address.street: Multiple venues in Alfama, Bairro Alto, and Lapa

directions.general: Fado restaurants located throughout historic Lisbon, concentrated in Alfama (traditional), Bairro Alto (bohemian), and Lapa (upscale)
directions.fromCruisePort: Many of Lisbon's fado houses are in Alfama, within 5-15 minutes on foot of the terminal; the listing's reference point is about 250 m away. After a late show, a taxi back to the ship takes a few minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro to Santa Apolónia or Terreiro do Paço, then walk to Alfama. Tram 28 stops near several fado houses. Taxis recommended for evening shows
directions.parking: Very limited in Alfama - not recommended. Taxi or rideshare strongly advised

openingTimes.currentStatus: Most fado houses open in the evening; days and hours vary by house

seasonal.hours: Dinner from about 19:30–20:00; fado from about 20:30–21:00 until midnight or later
seasonal.notes: Check the house you book: some close one evening a week, and timings differ.

closedDates: Varies by house: check when booking

admissionPrices.notes: No single price: each house sets its own. Established Alfama houses charge a set menu that includes the fado; in 2026 Parreirinha de Alfama publishes €68 per person (paid from age 6) and Clube de Fado €78 per person, drinks extra. Smaller tascas usually charge a minimum spend per person instead. Ask the price, and whether drinks are included, before sitting down.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 2.5–3 hours for dinner and the first sets; longer if you stay to closing
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Arrive at the start of dinner service (about 19:30–20:00) so you have eaten before the first set. Book ahead for summer and weekend evenings.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Book ahead. Ask whether the price is a set menu or a minimum spend, and whether drinks are included. Stay silent during each song and applaud at the end; talk and order between sets. Avoid places recruiting diners in the street.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: 3–4 hours in the evening, plus 5–15 minutes' walk each way to most Alfama houses
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Most Alfama houses are a short but uphill walk from the terminal on cobbles and steps, and many occupy old buildings with steps inside. A taxi can usually get close; ask the house about access when booking.
tips: Check your all-aboard time first: singing usually starts between 20:30 and 21:00 and runs past midnight.
Ask the price per person before you sit down, and whether it is a set menu or a minimum spend.
In 2026, established Alfama houses publish set menus of about €68–78 per person including the fado; drinks may be extra.
Book a day or more ahead in summer and at weekends: good houses have small rooms.
Stay silent during each song with your phone away, applaud at the end, and talk between sets.
Walk past places that send staff into the street to recruit diners for 'fado shows'.
Most Alfama houses are 5–15 minutes' walk from the terminal; the way back is downhill, or a short taxi ride late at night.
If your ship leaves before evening, visit the Fado Museum near the terminal instead (Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–18:00, €5).

highlights: Live fado with Portuguese guitar and classical guitar, in sets between the courses
Set menu that includes the performance at established houses (about €68–78 in 2026)
Cheaper fado vadio in small tascas, usually on a minimum spend
Many Alfama houses within 5–15 minutes' walk of the cruise terminal
Silence during each song: the main rule in any serious house
Fado Museum near the terminal for daytime context

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Many fado houses occupy old buildings with steps and narrow rooms, on steep, cobbled Alfama streets. Ask the house about access when booking; a taxi can usually drop you close by.
